steps.title: Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have you felt since finishing our neuropathy program? I usually hear one of three things. Symptoms are under control, starting to return, or pretty much back. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes care with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Symptoms Starting to Return
steps.content:
Thanks for telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. Nerve symptoms can return after the program ends. Your notes say you were doing well when you finished. Does that sound right?

(Let them confirm.)

steps.title: Symptoms Fully Back
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Nerve symptoms can return after the program ends. Your notes say you were doing well when you finished. What do you think brought them back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask a few questions about any symptoms you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{complaint_reference}} is starting to return. We'll come back to that. First, can I ask a few questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every symptom they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you noticed any burning or tingling?

Any numbness?

Any trouble with your balance?

Are nerve symptoms disrupting your sleep?

Any cramping or weakness in your hands or legs?

Are you taking any medications for these symptoms?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Questions: Symptoms Returning
steps.content:
(Write down every symptom they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you noticed any burning or tingling?

Any numbness?

Any trouble with your balance?

Are nerve symptoms disrupting your sleep?

Any cramping or weakness in your hands or legs?

Are you taking any medications for these symptoms?

Including {{complaint_reference}}, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask three quick questions about {{main_concern}}. This will help me update your file.

(Ask each question in order. Let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It sounds like this has been hard on you.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. Do not argue. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why They Stopped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still doing well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in for check-ins?

(Let them answer. Do not argue.)

Regular check-ins help us watch for changes in your nerve symptoms.

(Tap the reason they shared.)

steps.title: Objection: Symptoms Came Back
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's one of the most common reasons people call us back.

How long after the program ended did you notice it again?

(Let them answer.)

Nerves heal slowly, and they don't always hold on their own once the sessions stop. Care ended a little early, or something in your day started pulling on it again. Either way, you're not back at square one. You already did the hard part once.

We'd rather have {{provider_name}} check it now than let it settle back in. You'll hear where things stand and what it would take.

Can we get you in for a look?

steps.title: Objection: Frustrated It Returned
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. You put in the work, and it's frustrating to feel it slip.

Is it the same as before, or has it changed, like new spots or worse at night?

(Let them answer. Do not defend the program.)

The frustration usually comes from not knowing why. Sometimes {{main_concern}} comes back because the nerves needed more time than the program gave them. Sometimes something else changed, like a new medication or your overall health. Those have different answers, and guessing from home won't tell you which one it is.

A visit with {{provider_name}} tells you why, and that's the part that takes the frustration out of it. If we can't help this time, you'll hear that too.

Would knowing why make it easier?

steps.title: Objection: Bad Experience
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm sorry that happened.

Can I ask what the experience was, so I can pass it along?

(Let them answer. Do not argue or explain it away. Do not give medical advice.)

Thank you. {{provider_name}} will want to hear that directly, and that's a fair reason to come in on its own. You'd be sitting down to talk about what happened and where {{main_concern}} stands now. Nothing is done at that visit unless you want it done.

If you'd rather not continue after that, we'll respect it. You'd still leave knowing where things stand.

Would you be comfortable coming in just to talk?

steps.title: Reason: Feeling Fine
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When you feel good, a check-in stops feeling urgent. Regular visits help us watch for changes.

Is there anything else that kept you from coming in?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule for a check-in. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. A check-in is one visit, and you're not committing to treatment.

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Is there anything else that kept you from coming in?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule for a check-in. Would that work?

steps.title: Reason: Life Got Busy
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and check-ins get pushed down the list. We can work around your schedule.

Is there anything else that kept you from coming in?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find an easy time for your check-in. Does that seem fair?

steps.title: Reason: Waiting for Symptoms
steps.content:
That's a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}. A check-in helps us look for changes before symptoms disrupt your day.

Is there anything else that kept you from coming in?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a check-in on the schedule. Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Reason: Moved or Changed Providers
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're still nearby, we'd be glad to see you again. Your history is already in your file.

Is there anything else that kept you from coming in?

(If another reason comes up, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Would that be okay?

steps.title: Transition: Symptoms Fully Back
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{complaint_reference}} is pretty much back. We'll come back to that. First, can I ask a few questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Symptoms Fully Back
steps.content:
(Write down every symptom they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you noticed any burning or tingling?

Any numbness?

Any trouble with your balance?

Are nerve symptoms disrupting your sleep?

Any cramping or weakness in your hands or legs?

Are you taking any medications for these symptoms?

Including {{complaint_reference}}, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like a specialist, medication, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all help, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is how much nerve function is left to work with. {{provider_name}} already has your history and knows how you responded last time, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it more the cost of the visit itself, or not knowing what insurance will cover?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Insurance changes every year, so a lot of people aren't sure what they have now. Our front desk can check your coverage before you come in, so there are no surprises. And this first visit is one appointment, not another program. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about coming in a lot like before?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that's a handful of visits to settle it down. Sometimes it's more, and you'll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing you up for a whole program on the phone.

We have early and late openings. Since you've been here before, the first visit is usually under 30 minutes.

Could you find half an hour for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that it's back and you don't know why. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: Needs Time to Think
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} has been going on for a while now. It's had time to sort itself out on its own, and it hasn't. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: Send Information
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you how much of {{main_concern}} can still be helped. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at you, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
